introduction: Delaware Healthy Children Program offers low-cost health coverage for eligible uninsured children. Applications are also checked for Medicaid eligibility.
description: Delaware Healthy Children Program offers low-cost health coverage for eligible uninsured children. Applications are also checked for Medicaid eligibility.

sections.who: Children must be younger than 19, live in Delaware and meet income, status and coverage conditions. Comprehensive existing insurance can affect eligibility; ask before cancelling a policy.
sections.get: DHCP provides children’s health coverage with family premium conditions. A child eligible for Medicaid is enrolled through that pathway instead.
sections.docs:
• Family income, including self-employment tax records where applicable.
  • Child identity and requested status information.
  • Details of current or recently ended health insurance.
sections.apply:
1. Apply through ASSIST

    Use ASSIST, or request help and a paper application at 800-996-9969.

  2. Submit the requested records

    Provide income and coverage information and any further evidence requested.

  3. Review the coverage decision

    Confirm whether the child qualifies for Medicaid or DHCP and what payment or plan arrangements apply.
sections.after: Keep renewal letters and premium instructions. Ask about consequences before voluntarily dropping existing coverage.
sections.sources: Content checked October 1, 2026 using DHCP eligibility and application; ASSIST application. Current eligibility and the final decision remain with the program.

faqs: Is a child with insurance automatically eligible?
No. Existing comprehensive coverage affects DHCP eligibility.
Will the child be checked for Medicaid?
Yes. DHCP applications are screened for Medicaid.
Can I request a paper application?
Call 800-996-9969 or use the state forms link.
Should I cancel insurance to qualify?
Ask the program first; loss-of-coverage rules can affect eligibility.
